prose.intro_html:
Here is a dish that sounds like a splurge and cooks like a budget line item. Honey BBQ chicken over a blender cheese sauce that hugs every noodle, and it still lands at 751 calories with 50.5 grams of protein a serving. That is not a cheat meal pretending to be dinner. That is dinner doing the work of a cheat meal.

The trick is that the creamy part is not a stick of butter and a brick of cheese. It is cottage cheese and light cream cheese blended smooth with milk, so the richness is real but the fat stays at 24.4 grams. Then the chicken gets tossed in honey and BBQ sauce and caramelized just enough to taste like something you paid for. Fourteen containers, one afternoon, and lunch is handled for two weeks.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the pasta in the big bag. This batch wants 2 1/3 pounds dry, so a single one pound box will not carry you and a family size bag keeps the shelf stocked for the next round.

Chicken breast is the anchor at 3 pounds. Watch for the larger family or value pack, and dice it at home rather than paying for the pre-cut tray.

The cheese sauce leans on three dairy items working together: 2 1/3 cups fat free cottage cheese, about 3 cups of 1/3 fat cream cheese, and 4 3/4 cups shredded reduced fat cheddar. Shredding a block yourself is a small chore that pays you back, and store brand dairy performs the same once it is blended smooth. Grab 2 1/4 cups of milk while you are in that aisle.

The spice rack does most of the flavor here and costs almost nothing per batch: garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, dried parsley, black pepper, ground ginger, salt, and yellow mustard. Store brand jars are the move, and a jar lasts far past this recipe. Round it out with honey, BBQ sauce, and a can of low calorie cooking spray.
prose.make_it:
Season the diced chicken first. Toss the 3 pounds of chicken with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper until every piece is coated.

Cook it your way. Air fryer at 350F for 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until golden and cooked through. No air fryer, no problem: heat a non stick pan over medium, hit it with cooking spray, and cook the chicken 6 to 8 minutes until browned and done.

Now make it honey BBQ. Move the cooked chicken to a bowl and toss it with the honey and BBQ sauce until every piece is glossy, then return it to the heat for another 1 to 2 minutes so the sauce caramelizes a touch. Set it aside.

Boil the pasta in well salted water and cook to package directions. Before you drain, save about a quarter cup of the pasta water, then drain and set the noodles aside.

Build the sauce in a blender. Combine the cottage cheese, cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, dried parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and yellow mustard, and blend until smooth and creamy. Pour it into a saucepan over medium low heat and stir. If it stiffens up, loosen it with a splash of that reserved pasta water. Cook 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens and turns silky.

Fold the drained pasta into the sauce and stir to coat, adding a little more pasta water if you want it looser. Let the whole pot sit for 10 minutes so the flavors settle and the sauce grabs the noodles. Finish each serving with the honey BBQ chicken and a sprinkle of parsley.
prose.portion_html:
This recipe splits into 14 containers, so let the scale do the dividing instead of your eyeballs. Once the mac and cheese has rested, set your empty pot on a kitchen scale and zero it, weigh the full pot of cheesy pasta, then divide that number by 14. That is your gram target per container, and it makes all 14 land on the same 751 calories and 50.5 grams of protein.

Scoop the pasta to that weight in each container, then top every one with an equal share of the honey BBQ chicken so nobody opens a lunch that is all noodle and no protein. A final sprinkle of parsley and the lids go on.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Run the math and this comes out to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. For a bowl of honey BBQ chicken mac and cheese carrying over 40 grams of protein and staying under 800 calories, that is the kind of number that makes packing lunch feel less like discipline and more like a win.

Fourteen dinners built in one afternoon, priced like a side dish, eating like a treat. That is the whole idea.

head.description: Honey BBQ chicken mac and cheese meal prep for 14 servings, 751 calories and 50.5g protein each. A blender cottage cheese sauce keeps it creamy and lean on a budget.
head.keywords: honey bbq chicken mac and cheese, high protein mac and cheese, meal prep dinner, budget meal prep, cottage cheese mac and cheese, chicken pasta meal prep, high protein meal prep
steps: Toss the 3 pounds of diced chicken with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.

Cook the chicken in the air fryer at 350F for 10 to 12 minutes, shaking halfway, or in a non stick pan sprayed with cooking spray over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until cooked through and browned.
Transfer the chicken to a bowl, toss with the honey and BBQ sauce until coated, then return to the heat 1 to 2 minutes to caramelize the sauce. Set aside.
Boil the pasta in salted water to package directions. Reserve about 1/4 cup of pasta water, then drain and set aside.
In a blender, combine the cottage cheese, cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, dried parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and yellow mustard. Blend until smooth.
Pour the sauce into a saucepan over medium low heat, stirring. Loosen with a splash of reserved pasta water if it thickens too much, and cook 3 to 5 minutes until silky.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce and stir to coat, adding more pasta water to reach your desired consistency.
Let the mac and cheese rest 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the sauce thickens.
Portion across 14 containers by weight, top each with an equal share of the honey BBQ chicken, and garnish with parsley.
